key_insight: AnyRecon leverages a video diffusion model that conditions on arbitrary, unordered sparse input frames to synthesize geometrically consistent novel views, enabling scalable and more accurate 3D reconstruction from casual captures.
problem_solved: Improves sparse‑view 3D reconstruction by overcoming limited geometric consistency and poor scalability of prior diffusion-based methods that typically condition on only one or two capture frames.
method: Train a video diffusion generator that accepts arbitrary, unordered sparse frames as conditioning and produces temporally and spatially consistent novel-view sequences.
Aggregate multi-frame cues with a permutation‑invariant encoding strategy so the model scales to variable numbers and orders of input views.
Fuse synthesized novel views with multi‑view reconstruction / neural rendering to recover dense, consistent 3D geometry suitable for large or diverse scenes.
impact: Enables practitioners to reconstruct high-quality 3D from casual, sparse captures (phone photos or short clips) with better multi-view consistency and scalability—useful for AR/VR, mapping, and asset creation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: unordered sparse input frames → permutation‑invariant encoder → video diffusion → synthesized novel views → 3D reconstruction
Side‑by‑side comparison: reconstructions from 1–2 conditional frames versus AnyRecon (showing improved geometry and fewer artifacts)
Grid of synthesized novel views demonstrating temporal/spatial consistency across viewpoints
Bar chart or table of key quantitative gains (e.g., IoU / Chamfer or qualitative fidelity) to highlight improvements
paper_title: AnyRecon: Arbitrary-View 3D Reconstruction with Video Diffusion Model
paper_authors: Yutian Chen, Shi Guo, Renbiao Jin, Tianshuo Yang, Xin Cai
